problems.title: The released weighted shrinkage is not the proximal map
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, Eq.(4), PDF p.5; Algorithm 1, line 16, PDF p.21; models/clstm.py, lines 342–360
claim: For fixed positive normalized weights, the compression step should minimize \(J(U)=\tfrac12\|U-W\|_F^2+\sum_jt_j\|U_j\|_2\). The release instead divides a column by \(\max(\|W_j\|_2,\lambda\eta)\), even when its weighted threshold is smaller.
analysis: Take two columns \(W=(1/2,2)\), \(\lambda\eta=1\), and \(\alpha=(1/10,9/10)\), embedded in the allowed hidden dimension by zero padding. Grant the release’s threshold convention \(t=2\alpha=(1/5,9/5)\). It returns \((0.15,0.20)\), whereas columnwise soft thresholding gives \((0.30,0.20)\). The objective values are respectively \(2.07125\) and \(2.06\); the first-coordinate derivative at the release output is \(0.15-0.5+0.2=-0.15\), so the return is not the unique minimizer. Uniform weights are a passing special case.
result: The public nonuniform-weight operator differs from the correct printed formula. Its later optimization and benchmark effects are unmeasured.
assumptions: The two learned weights are positive and sum to one; the inspected default-threshold branch is used.
repair: Use \((1-t/r)_+w\) for \(r=\|w\|_2>0\), with zero output for a zero column. Cauchy–Schwarz reduces the objective to \(\tfrac12(s-r)^2+ts\), uniquely minimized by \(s=(r-t)_+\). Match the threshold scaling to the stated objective.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a release-only operator error; the paper’s mathematical proximal formula itself is correct.

problems.title: Cross-station normalization changes the channel histories
problems.source_location: Appendix C, Moléne description, PDF p.22; prepare_data.py, lines 66–84
claim: The released Moléne loader normalizes across stations at each time: \(Y_{j,t}=(X_{j,t}-\min_\ell X_{\ell,t})/(\max_\ell X_{\ell,t}-\min_\ell X_{\ell,t})\). A graph of these channels need not describe raw-station history relations.
analysis: Use independent stationary channels \(X_t=(0,U_t,1,M_t)\), with \(U_t\) iid uniform on \([1,2]\) and \(M_t=3+M_{t-1}/2+\eta_t\), where \(\eta_t\) is iid uniform on \([-1,1]\). Its stationary solution lies in \([4,8]\). No raw channel causes another. Normalization gives \(Y_t=(0,B_t,C_t,1)\), with \(B_t=U_t/M_t\) and \(C_t=1/M_t\). The marker history reveals the previous autoregressive state, and the conditional prediction is \[\mathbb E[B_t\mid M_{t-1}=m]=\frac34\log\frac{4+m/2}{2+m/2}.\] It is strictly decreasing, taking approximately \(0.275794\) at \(m=5\) and \(0.232616\) at \(m=7\).

Even given \(M_{t-2}=m_0\) and the complete earlier target history, observing \(B_{t-1}=b\) leaves the fresh state on the nontrivial interval \((a-1,a+1)\cap(1/b,2/b)\), where \(a=3+m_0/2\). Its conditional density is proportional to \(m\). Thus the strictly varying conditional prediction is not recoverable from the target’s entire history, while the marker reveals it. This establishes a newly created predictive relation, not merely one-step correlation.
result: The normalization is legitimate for a graph of relative temperatures. Inferring raw physical station relations requires a separate justification; no actual weather edge is disproved here.
assumptions: Independent stationary innovations and a nonzero normalization denominator hold throughout the construction.
repair: For raw-channel history preservation, fixed invertible channelwise affine transforms \(Y_{j,t}=a_jX_{j,t}+b_j\), \(a_j\ne0\), preserve each history sigma-field. Otherwise identify the target as the transformed-variable graph.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a bounded preprocessing/interpretation issue, not a counterexample to a stated normalization-invariance theorem.

problems.title: The public Lorenz generator uses a different observation protocol
problems.source_location: Appendix C, Lorenz-96, PDF p.22; synthetic.py, lines 60–79; prepare_data.py, lines 93–97
claim: The paper specifies output spacing \(0.05\) and noise added at each simulation step. The loader retains the generator’s default \(\delta=0.1\), and the source adds noise after deterministic integration.
analysis: With \(N=T+B\) inclusive grid points from zero to \(N\delta\), actual output spacing is \(N\delta/(N-1)\). At \(T=500\) and \(B=1000\), this is \(150/1499\approx0.100067\). The separate post-integration addition makes observational noise: unlike \(z_{k+1}=az_k+\epsilon_k\), an earlier observation perturbation cannot propagate into a later deterministic state. If “each step” meant observational noise, that portion is descriptive ambiguity rather than a stochastic-model error.
result: The inspected generator does not match the reported spacing; noise placement is explicit in the source. Which version generated the published scores remains unresolved.
repair: Pin the historical generator and choose output times \(t_k=k\Delta\) for the intended spacing. Specify observational versus process noise before any experiment revision; an arbitrary stochastic-solver substitution is not justified.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: This is experiment-method correspondence with no established effect on the historical rankings.

problems.title: The release does not honor the described batch and optimizer settings
problems.source_location: Section 4, Training and Evaluation Details, PDF p.7; models/clstm.py, lines 497–568; F40T500.yaml
claim: The paper describes full-batch Adam, weight decay \(0.1\), learning-rate warmup \(2000\) and coefficient warmup \(1500\). The public path uses replacement minibatches and constructs AdamW without forwarding the declared decay.
analysis: The sampler requests \(256\,\mathrm{max\_iter}\) replacement draws and the loader hardcodes batch size \(256\), regardless of the exposed argument. With \(T=500\), context \(10\) and stride \(1\), there are \(490\) windows, so such an update is not full batch. The optimizer call forwards only learning rate; logging a decay value in extra keyword arguments does not apply it. The released configuration uses warmup \(2200\) and coefficient start \(2000\). Generic minibatch pseudocode does not resolve the explicit full-batch experimental description.
result: These are distinct reproducibility settings. Neither stochastic optimization nor AdamW is intrinsically invalid, and published-result correspondence is not established.
repair: Expose and forward the selected optimizer parameters, honor an explicit full-batch or minibatch mode, and retain the resolved experiment configuration. No replacement training run is validated.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is described; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The findings concern public training configuration, without evidence that the original reported models used the discrepant path.
